head: claude/mi90-avax-venue-max-resolution
title: MI-90: AVAX venue-max resolution — verified against a real venue read (Tier-2/3, PROPOSAL)
body:
## Verdict: the recovered diff is CORRECT. Carrying it forward, with three corrections.

This takes ownership of the work preserved on **#10780** (`[RECOVERED — DO NOT MERGE]`), which carried **no review, no verification and no tier gate**. It was an unattributed proposal from a sub-session that died without committing. I read it adversarially, expecting to discard it. It holds up.

**#10780 should be closed** — a preservation branch is not a disposition. This PR supersedes it and preserves its three commits in history, so the dead session's authorship is not erased.

---

## Why the bug is real — verified in code, not assumed

`AVAXUSDT` is **absent** from `precision._STATIC_LOT_RULE`, which holds `BTCUSDT`/`ETHUSDT`/`SOLUSDT` only. So on a live-lookup miss, AVAX falls through to the offline `InstrumentProfile`, which on `main` has no `max_qty` field at all → `venue_max=None` → the clamp, keyed on `venue_max is not None`, is **skipped**. That is the entire third-occurrence defect, and it is one line.

## Reproduced through the REAL resolution path

Run against `main`'s source, the recovered test produces:

```
LegalizedQty(qty=22995.1, ok=True, venue_min=0.1, step=0.1,
             source='instrument_profile', venue_max=None,
             clamped=False, qty_str='22995.1')
```

Byte-identical to the payload the venue bounced.

**This is the part that matters most.** The pre-existing suite `tests/test_qty_legalize_venue_max.py` monkeypatches `_resolve_venue_lot_rule` to return a rule that *already carries* `vmax=22_000`, so every case enters the clamp branch. It tests the **clamp**, which was correct all along, and never the **resolution**, which is where `venue_max` actually goes `None`. That is how this bug reached a third recurrence with green tests throughout.

The recovered `tests/test_qty_legalize_venue_max_resolution.py` does **not** repeat that mistake — it fakes at the `get_instruments_info` **client boundary**, so resolution genuinely runs. I verified this rather than taking it on faith: **all 6 of its tests fail on `main`** and pass here.

## Real venue read (not a fixture)

Live VM journal, `ict-trader-live.service`, via `/api/diag/journalctl`, `2026-09-02T09:06:11Z`:

```
_submit_order(bybit): The number of contracts exceeds maximum limit allowed:
too large, order_qty:2299510000000 > max_qty:2200000000000 (ErrCode: 10001)

POST .../v5/order/create {"symbol": "AVAXUSDT", "qty": "22995.1",
                          "tpSize": "22995.1", "slSize": "22995.1", ...}
```

`2200000000000 / 1e8 = 22000`. **The venue itself names the ceiling**, so `config/instruments.yaml max_qty: 22000` is MEASURED, not guessed.

Corroborating, from `/api/diag/journal?table=trades` — POPULATION: 60 most recent trade rows, 8 on AVAXUSDT: trade `id 5367` (2026-09-02T17:41:51Z, `ict_scalp_avax_5m`) **filled** at `position_size: 21657.1`. So 21,657.1 was accepted and 22,995.1 was rejected, bracketing the cap. 22,000 sits inside that bracket.

---

## What I changed on top of the recovered diff

### 1. A false claim on the order path, removed

The recovered comment asserted a stale ceiling *"can only ever under-size (clamping lower than the current cap), never place an illegal order."* **That is false.** Both directions are reachable:

| venue moves | we do | result |
|---|---|---|
| RAISES its cap | clamp low | under-size (benign) |
| **LOWERS its cap** | clamp to a ceiling it no longer honours | **order still rejected** |

No worse than today's unclamped behaviour, but *"never illegal"* is an overclaim. A stale ceiling **narrows** the bug; it does not close it. An over-confident comment on the order path is the same failure mode as the collapsed state it sits beside — and this repo's whole lesson here is that a confident-but-wrong statement is what licenses the next recurrence.

### 2. Provenance of the 22,000, recorded — it was measured on the DEMO venue

The rejection log line names the wire target as **`api-demo.bybit.com`**, and `config/accounts.yaml` carries **`demo: true`** on `bybit_1`. So the ceiling is real and venue-published, but published by Bybit's **demo** venue.

**Correctly scoped today, and only today.** POPULATION: all 3 bybit accounts in `config/accounts.yaml`. `AVAXUSDT` appears in `bybit_1`'s symbols **only**; `bybit_2` — the sole account with no `demo` flag — lists `BTCUSDT`/`ETHUSDT`/`XRPUSDT`/`ADAUSDT`. Every AVAX order reaches the same demo venue the ceiling was measured on.

But `max_qty` is **symbol**-scoped, not account-scoped. Adding `AVAXUSDT` to `bybit_2` is a one-line config edit that would silently promote a demo-measured number into a **production** fallback ceiling never measured on production. Filed as `BL-20260903-AVAX-VENUE-MAX-CEILING-MEASURED-ON-DEMO-BUT-SYMBOL-SCOPED` (low, latent) — **not fixed here**, because fixing it means making `max_qty` account-scoped, which is a design change well outside this object.

### 3. The untested precedence rule, covered

The recovered suite tested each source in isolation but **never asserted the authority order** the entire fix turns on. Two tests added:

- **`test_live_published_ceiling_outranks_the_profile`** — live says 9000, profile says 22000 → the venue wins. Were this backwards, a stale profile ceiling would quietly replace the venue's own current answer on every order.
- **`test_a_live_absent_ceiling_is_not_overridden_by_the_profile`** — the direction that actually bites. The ceiling-only cross-consult fires on `could_not_look` **only**. Were it ever widened to `absent`, a stale profile would start clamping orders the venue would have accepted — opening exactly the new-refusal blast radius the fix's own comments promise never to open.

Both pass, so the implemented precedence is correct; they lock it.

---

## Evidence: tests and guards

**Order-path set** (12 files touching `qty_legalize` / `precision` / `instrument_profile` / `profile_loader`):

| | passed | failed |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 215 | 10 |
| this branch | **223** | 10 |

The 10 failures are **identical on both** — `tests/test_ib_sizing_and_data.py` (Interactive Brokers), unrelated to this change. I diffed the failing test *names*, not just the counts: **no branch-only failures**. Both venue-max suites green (8 + 15).

**Guards**: `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` → **PASS 53 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 18**, run after committing. `layer-guard` needed `import-linter`, which I installed rather than reporting unrun: 6 contracts kept, 0 broken.

### ⚠️ What I could NOT run — not reported as green

- **110 test files** requiring `pandas` / `numpy` / `fastapi` / `httpx` / `ccxt`, absent from this container (confirmed pre-existing collection errors on `main`, not caused by this diff). I installed `pandas`/`numpy` partway through and re-baselined both sides to keep the comparison honest.
- **No live venue instruments-info read.** Bybit's public API is geo-blocked from this sandbox (CloudFront 403), and no `/api/diag/*` route exposes lot bounds. The venue evidence above is the venue's own **rejection text** plus an accepted-fill bracket — strong, but it is not a direct read of `lotSizeFilter.maxOrderQty`. **If the operator wants the ceiling confirmed by direct read before merge, that is a reasonable gate and I did not clear it.**

---

## Tier — this is a PROPOSAL, not a merge request

The order path (`execute.py`, `qty_legalize.py`, `precision.py`) is **Tier-2/3** per `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` § Permission Tiers. I prepared and validated; **the merge is the operator's**. No account-mode, risk-cap, sizing-formula or strategy-config change. No self-merge. Draft, deliberately.

### Behaviour change, stated plainly

Orders that previously went out **unclamped** on a `could_not_look` resolution will now be **clamped** when the other source publishes a ceiling. Today that is **AVAXUSDT only** — it is the sole symbol with `max_qty` in `instruments.yaml`. Additionally, `_submit_order` now emits a `WARNING` per order on `could_not_look` (every non-Bybit venue, and Bybit lookup misses) and a `debug` on `absent`. The `absent` path is deliberately `debug`, not `warn` — a warning on the common path is the desensitised-alarm failure mode.

**No new refusals are added.** `could_not_look` places the order and says so; it does not block. That is the correct call: refusing on an unresolved ceiling would start blocking orders that are legal today, a far larger blast radius than the bug.

---

## Disposition of #10780

Close it. This PR supersedes it, keeps its commits in history, and gives the work the review, verification and tier gate it never had.
